Shared rules made the system reusable beyond one team or screen

I led a component audit, structured foundations and reusable layers, introduced controlled editing rights and aligned the component roadmap with engineering. Knowledge-sharing and retrospectives kept design decisions connected across functions.

In the Credit Suisse project, I focused on enhancing user experience and optimizing design processes. I defined key metrics and goals for both the design system and team, developed a flexible framework for simple creation of Customer Journey Maps (CJMs) for Marketing Department, and contributed to Competitor Analysis. My role included creating and updating components with a new brand visual style, collaborating with Frontify for documentation, and improving design workflows. This project allowed me to refine the Design System and foster better cross-departmental collaboration.
Creation of new and reworking of old components with a new brand visual language. Creating a Specification for a Component to pass it to Development.

I worked on creating new components as well as redesigning existing components to align them with the brand's fresh visual language. Working closely with the design team and brand stakeholders, we developed visually cohesive components that embodied the essence of the brand. In addition, I created specifications that ensure consistent implementation of these components across platforms, allowing us to create a consistent user experience for users.

To streamline the component documentation process, I leveraged the capabilities of Frontify. By utilizing Frontify I described and documented components, including design guidelines, usage instructions, and visual examples. This centralized approach enabled seamless collaboration among the design team, developers, and stakeholders, ensuring clarity and consistency in component usage throughout the organization. Direct connection from Figma to Frontify

Metrics played a crucial role in measuring our activities and progress. By establishing key performance indicators, we were able to track the impact of our initiatives and identify areas for improvement within the design system. Throughout the project, I actively collaborated with stakeholders, designers, and crossfunctional teams, fostering a culture of transparency, open communication, and knowledge sharing.
Creating a matrix to understand how mature a design system is.

One of the notable achievements of the project was the creation of a flexible framework for the creation of customer journey maps (CJM) for the Marketing department. This is a simple but convenient and flexible framework for creating a customer journey, where a marketer can customize phases or swap them if needed, as well as enter all the necessary data and numbers.

During this project, the Explore Team worked on updating important parts of the Qatar Airways website to improve the user experience and business outcomes. The redesign included the homepage, Privilege Club, Destination page, and key widgets like booking, COVID-19 info, and Qmiles management. The main goal was to make the user journey smoother, improve the content structure, and create easy entry points for users.
Team
3 Designers (L3™L5 L5)
Activities
Design System Experience Design Visual Design Collaboration Presentation

After the redesign, we closely tracked metrics to see how the changes affected both the users and the business. Through workshops with the development team and Business Analyst, we came up with innovative ideas, making sure they were technically possible. Usability testing provided important feedback, which helped us improve the design even more.

After analyzing the situation, I determined that altering existing components would require excessive effort from the development team. To introduce the new branding effectively, I focused on redesigning the Hero Section, the first element users see on the page. Using the project designer's UX prototypes as a foundation, I created Hero Sections for the Article, Team, and Match pages. I also made minor adjustments to existing components to ensure overall consistency with the new brand identity.
Develop concepts for redesigning the site's pages, taking into account the new branding, with minimal changes in existing components.
Proper Delivery of all working files to the Client, including components, pages and style guides.

At the end of the project, I developed over 20 complex composite components, 4 page templates, and generated ideas for future redesigns, pending current restrictions. I collaborated with the design manager from OneFootball to organize these into two Figma files: one for the Style Guide, which included instructions, design language, components, icons, and assets; and another, Consumer Web - Templates, for redesigned pages across all breakpoints. The components in the Style Guide were designed to be flexible, supporting both dark and light themes, and optimized for various devices.
Look Like is an Innovative mobile App Designed to Make the Process of Learning English Enjoyable and Effective Through the Integration of Mnemonic Rules.

Art Director, Experience Designer

In developing an English learning app, I focused on creating a user-friendly, visually engaging experience. I designed an intuitive interface with clean graphics and simple navigation, making it accessible for all proficiency levels. To enhance organization, I used color-coded decks and incorporated interactive games to keep users motivated. The design balances functionality and aesthetics, encouraging regular use and supporting continuous language improvement.

We engaged in an extensive discussion about the mechanics of language learning, focusing on how to translate the tangible experience of using physical flashcards into the digital space. To achieve this, I developed prototypes for usability testing, allowing us to assess the effectiveness of our proposed mechanics with real users.
I started by gathering requirements and drafting a design brief, discussing the brand and understanding the principles of learning through mnemonic rules.

Additionally, I designed the Onion-[kuk] mascot, which played a crucial role in adding emotional engagement, gamification, and motivation to the app. This mascot was also integral to our brand identity, serving as a central figure in user communication across onboarding, training, storytelling, and marketing initiatives.
